result.summary: Disconnect peers that send a sendtxrcncl P2P message after verack, regardless of whether -txreconciliation is enabled. Previously, nodes running with -txreconciliation disabled ignored post-verack sendtxrcncl messages instead of disconnecting the misbehaving peer.
result.problem: Nodes running with transaction reconciliation disabled do not enforce BIP 330 disconnection requirements when receiving a sendtxrcncl message after verack, violating the protocol specification.
evidence: PR description: 'As mandated by BIP 330... always disconnect such a peer, regardless of the value of -txreconciliation. Previously the code would ignore and not disconnect such a peer if -txreconciliation=0.'
result.card: Enforces BIP 330 compliance by unconditionally disconnecting peers that send a sendtxrcncl message after verack. Previously, nodes with -txreconciliation=0 would ignore the message instead of disconnecting the peer. This aligns peer handling with the BIP specification regardless of whether local transaction reconciliation is toggled on.

risk.why: A bug in P2P message handling or peer disconnection logic could cause nodes to disconnect well-behaved peers during handshake negotiation.
